Summary: Milestone 1: Initial Release - Core GC Analyzer
Epic Name: Milestone 1: Initial Release - Core GC Analyzer
Description: Initial commit establishing GC Analyzer: baseline fleet monitoring app with performance and logo optimizations. Commit: d13dade.

Summary: SSH-based GC log collection service
Epic Link: Milestone 1: Initial Release - Core GC Analyzer
Description: Implemented gcanalyzer/collector.py to connect to Kafka broker/controller and ZooKeeper hosts over SSH and pull GC log files (kafkaServer-gc.log and rotated variants) for local parsing, removing the need for manual log retrieval.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Collector connects to remote hosts via SSH using per-node config (host/user/key) defined in cluster YAML
- Retrieves current + rotated GC log files (.log, .log.0-.4) for broker, controller, and ZooKeeper roles
- SSH/auth/network failures are surfaced rather than silently swallowed
- Sample log fixtures (samples/*.log) exist for local testing without live SSH access

Summary: GC log parsing engine for Kafka & ZooKeeper
Epic Link: Milestone 1: Initial Release - Core GC Analyzer
Description: gcanalyzer/parser.py parses raw JVM GC log lines (young/mixed/full GC, pause times, heap before/after) from Kafka 2.8.1-style unified logs and ZooKeeper logs into structured metric events.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Parses young, mixed, and Full GC events with timestamp, pause duration, and heap before/after
- Handles both broker/controller and ZooKeeper log formats
- Unit tests (tests/test_pipeline.py) validate parsing against sample logs
- Malformed or partial log lines are skipped without crashing the pipeline

Summary: GC event analysis & fleet health scoring engine
Epic Link: Milestone 1: Initial Release - Core GC Analyzer
Description: gcanalyzer/analyzer.py and gcanalyzer/store.py aggregate parsed GC metrics into per-instance windows and compute a health score (healthy/watch/critical) plus derived findings (throughput %, p99 pause, Full GC count).
Acceptance Criteria:
- score_health() classifies an instance's rolling-window metrics into a health tier
- derive_findings() surfaces human-readable issues (e.g. high pause p99, frequent Full GCs)
- Metrics persist to a local SQLite-backed store (store.py) for later trend queries
- Covered by tests/test_fleet.py

Summary: Multi-cluster fleet topology & YAML configuration
Epic Link: Milestone 1: Initial Release - Core GC Analyzer

Acceptance Criteria:
- Cluster YAML supports region/env/cluster grouping and per-node SSH connection details
- build_fleet()/build_cluster() assemble a tree of clusters -> nodes with current health per node
- Example and demo cluster YAML files (BLUE-PROD, ONPREM-PROD, demo, demo1, test-demo-cluster) ship as references
- Config changes are picked up without code changes (YAML-driven)

Summary: Milestone 2: Fleet Health & Reliability Fixes
Description: Stabilization pass on fleet health evaluation and local tooling: fixed baseline health fallback edge cases, captured SSH stderr for permission issues, and made start-local.command robust across Python 3.10+ interpreters. Commits: c08a00d, 58da8b0, 367a350, 17c4eb6.

Summary: Fix fleet build health baseline evaluation edge case
Epic Link: Milestone 2: Fleet Health & Reliability Fixes
Description: build_fleet() and build_cluster() in gcanalyzer/fleet.py computed a health score from the trailing 24h metric window only; if a node had no rows in that window (e.g. after a quiet period) but did have a most-recent snapshot, health silently came back as unknown instead of falling back to the last known reading. Commit c08a00d.
Acceptance Criteria:
- When the 24h window has no rows but a last-known snapshot exists, health falls back to a single-point window built from that last row
- Both build_fleet() and build_cluster() apply the same fallback consistently
- No regression for nodes with normal, populated 24h windows

Summary: Robust Python 3.10+ interpreter selection in start-local.command
Epic Link: Milestone 2: Fleet Health & Reliability Fixes
Description: start-local.command hardened its interpreter discovery so the app reliably launches with a supported Python (3.10+) across differing local machine setups instead of failing on an incompatible default python/python3. Commit 58da8b0.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Script probes available Python interpreters and selects the first that satisfies the >=3.10 requirement
- Clear error message is shown if no compatible interpreter is found, rather than a raw traceback
- Works unmodified across the maintainer's tested local environments

Summary: Capture & log SSH stderr to bubble up permission issues
Epic Link: Milestone 2: Fleet Health & Reliability Fixes
Description: gcanalyzer/collector.py's SSH execution path now captures and logs stderr output from remote commands, so permission errors (e.g. denied log file access) are visible in job logs instead of failing silently. Commit 367a350.
Acceptance Criteria:
- stderr from remote SSH commands is captured alongside stdout
- Non-empty stderr is surfaced in collection logs / job output
- Permission-denied and similar SSH failures are diagnosable from the UI/log output without server-side debugging

Summary: Fix current_snapshot baseline health fallback edge case
Epic Link: Milestone 2: Fleet Health & Reliability Fixes
Description: gcanalyzer/store.py's current_snapshot() had the same 24h-window-empty-but-last-known-row-exists gap as fleet.py; fixed to reuse the last snapshot as a one-row window so instance detail pages don't show a blank health state. Commit 17c4eb6.
Acceptance Criteria:
- current_snapshot() returns a populated health/metrics block when a last row exists even if the 24h window is empty
- Instance detail view no longer shows 'no data' immediately after a quiet period
- Consistent behavior with the fleet/cluster-level fallback shipped alongside c08a00d
